free_tier.stated: 'When you sign up for CockroachDB Cloud, your new organization's account starts with $400 in free credits, allowing you to try the product at no cost.' The page states no trial length.

per_object_cap.stated: 10 GiB storage per organization on the recurring allowance; no per-object cap is published

retention.stated: trial credits last until used or expired; without a payment method, a 30-day grace period follows in which clusters are throttled and cannot be reconfigured, then all clusters in the organization are deleted and cannot be restored
retention.notes: the 30 days is the post-trial grace period before deletion, counted from the day the last credit is used or the credit expires, not from account creation; adding a payment method during the grace period fully restores the clusters

egress.terms: data transfer leaving the cluster is billed separately and the free-trial and Basic plan pages publish no included transfer allowance and no per-GB rate; recorded as a gap after checking both

interface_detail: the Postgres wire protocol with CockroachDB extensions; a Cloud API and the cockroach CLI
tooling: psql-compatible clients, the cockroach CLI, the Cloud API
chaining: the only free tier above 10 GiB of card-free-capable relational storage, if the card question resolves in your favour

limits.value: USD 400 of credits, with no published expiry

identity_cost.detail: GitHub, Google, Microsoft or an email address and password; a name, company and email verification on the email path; a payment method only at the end of the trial

reliability_note: no inactivity power-off; Request Unit consumption scales to zero when the cluster is idle. The trial path ends in an unrecoverable deletion 30 days after the credits run out without a payment method
confidence_note: two first-party pages were read on 2026-10-23: the free-trial page for the credits, the grace period and the deletion sentence, and the Basic plan page for scale-to-zero and the storage-limit behaviour. The deletion after the grace period is unrecoverable, which the word 'interruption' would understate.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'your new organization's account starts with $400 in free credits' and 'If the trial ends and a payment method has not been provided, a 30 day grace period begins.'
quoted: Standard '$0.092 per vCPU-hour', footer 'Standard from $0.057 / vCPU-hr' (the page contradicts itself), Mission Critical $0.162
a 30 day grace period follows the trial when no payment method is added, in which clusters are throttled and cannot be reconfigured, and all clusters are then deleted and cannot be restored

If the end of the grace period is reached and no payment method has been added, all clusters in the organization are deleted. Deleted clusters can not be restored.

notes: The pricing page carries two different Standard rates and prices the product as 'Cockroach Continuum' from 2026-09-15. RAM is never stated. No arbitrary process can be hosted; the credit buys a managed database.
binding_note: the request-unit counter throttles and the storage cap refuses writes, but both are recoverable. The 30-day deletion after the trial credits end is not: it removes every cluster in the organization and the page states they cannot be restored.
limits_note: the trial length is not published; the 30 days in retention.days is the post-trial grace period before deletion, not a trial length

extras.rate_conflict: the Standard card reads USD 0.092 per vCPU-hour and the footer table reads 'Standard from $0.057 / vCPU-hr' on the same page
